submission.bindingBasis: The planning-time source state digest (sha256:e5d8...) mismatches the current source state digest (sha256:79bc...). The owner contract requires compare-and-close against one exact expected digest; the old planning digest is now stale. Though the tree bytes are identical, the digest changed due to an empty commit (head revision moved from 4e6ce637... to cc96f434...). The contract allows a caller to re-observe and then close against the new exact current digest.
submission.rationale: Planner bound to the old digest e5d8...; the current digest is 79bc.... The owner contract's close is compare-and-close against one exact expected digest — a mismatched digest fails not_committed (as the planningBindingAttempt already shows REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed). The sole concurrent change was an empty Git commit that shifted the head revision and source digest even though the tree bytes are identical. The contract explicitly permits re-observation and then closing against the new exact current digest. Since the tree bytes are identical, after a fresh observation the new digest would match and close could proceed. I must not fabricate the re-observed digest or bind to a digest I haven't observed, so the correct move is to re-observe and then decide.
